scientific_formal.formal_expression:
```text
Team(t) => CollectiveIdentity(t)
purpose(t) != empty
owner_route(t) != empty

active(t) => exists p, m:
  Person(p)
  and TeamMembership(m)
  and binds(m, p, t)
  and current(m)

members(t, time_1) != members(t, time_2) =/=> t_at_time_1 != t_at_time_2
holds(team_or_person, role) =/=> authorized_for(team_or_person, action)
owns_responsibility(team_or_person, r) =/=> authority_grant(r)
```

Here `t` is the Team identity, `p` is a Person, and `m` is an independently
lifecycle-managed membership relation. Team membership, role assignment,
responsibility ownership, and authority are related but non-equivalent facts.
scientific_formal.normative_statement:
Team is the normalized definition identified by semantic.team, owned within scope.people-teams, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D69 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Team is a durable, owner-qualified collective identity through which Persons coordinate toward one declared purpose and scope, independently of its changing memberships, roles, responsibilities, and authority relations.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Team is a durable, owner-qualified collective identity through which Persons
coordinate toward one declared purpose and scope. Its identity, lifecycle,
membership, roles, responsibilities, and authority relationships are explicit
and remain separate.

A Team is not merely the current set of its members. Membership changes do not
silently create a different Team while its identity, purpose, scope, and owner
boundary remain stable. An active Team has at least one current Person
membership. A proposed Team may exist before its first membership so its
purpose and owner can be reviewed without inventing members.

In CyberAlchemy v2, traceability turns the stable repository objective into a

For a work object `x` and a review question `q`, traceability holds when there

```text
trace_q(x) = x -> link_1 -> link_2 -> ... -> answer_or_residue
```

Each `link_i` must have a target, relation type, and authority posture. If the
path breaks, the break must be recorded as typed residue or a named gap.

relation types, authority postures, and residue markers to be traversed without

boundaries: A connection is an allowed ordered pair of endpoint kinds in one exact Relation Kind contract; it is not a relation instance between two identified objects.
A source-kind list and target-kind list are discovery projections only; their Cartesian product is not a connection contract.
Registering or admitting an endpoint kind creates no connection.
A global connection cannot become effective until both endpoint kinds resolve to admitted carriers or to explicitly governed internal record contracts permitted by the Relation Kind.
Every global connection binds an exact qualifier schema and the allowed qualifier values and constraints for that ordered pair.
Every proposal declares global or ontology-local scope. An ontology-local connection remains inside its exact Ontology contract and does not enter the global Relation Kind registry by implication.

A specialized relation carrier declares one canonical-authority mapping: projects-as when the specialized carrier is canonical, or represented-by when the generic Typed Relation is canonical. Dual writable authority is forbidden.
Every effective connection binds an exact contestability contract and owner route for the Relation Kind, pair, qualifiers, endpoints, and relation instance.
The successor proposal resolves the effective predecessor Relation Kind version through decision and succession overlays before computing the new closed pair set.
Admitting a connection neither admits its endpoint carriers nor creates, validates, admits, activates, or proves a relation instance.

Reusing an existing Relation Kind is permitted only when its unique semantic question and qualifier contract express the proposed connection without collapse; otherwise a distinct Relation Kind must be proposed.
A wildcard, catch-all endpoint, directory convention, observed historical use, shared label, or local ontology edge is not a declared global connection.
record.claim_ceiling: This candidate defines how a closed global Relation Kind endpoint contract may be extended and how ontology-local scope remains bounded. It does not admit this Definition, admit or modify a Relation Kind, authorize any endpoint pair, resolve endpoint carriers, admit qualifier schemas or relation instances, select runtime behavior, or grant authority.
residue_refs: Relation Kind owner review remains required for every existing and proposed endpoint pair.
No canonical Relation Kind Artifact Type or general Typed Relation carrier currently exists.
Qualifier schemas and pair-specific value domains remain unmaterialized.
Twenty-two current endpoint kinds still lack canonical carriers.
Global versus ontology-local scope and specialized-carrier authority must be selected per connection contract.

scope.applicability: Proposing one additional global ordered source endpoint kind to target endpoint kind connection under an existing Relation Kind, proposing a distinct Relation Kind when the semantic question differs, or proving that an ontology-local connection remains bounded to one exact Ontology contract.
exclusions: Creating relation instances or admitting endpoint carriers.
Inferring connections from separate source and target indexes.
Changing Relation Kind meaning through an endpoint extension.
Using wildcard or catch-all endpoint kinds.
Publishing ontology-local edges as global connections without a separate admitted global contract.
Treating a specialized binding and its Typed Relation projection as two writable authorities.
Treating candidate validation, structural conformance, or endpoint admission as connection admission.

examples: Adding decision -> intent to relation.declares-effect-on preserves that Relation Kind question only when a closed effect_kind domain such as satisfies, rejects, or supersedes is bound to the exact pair.
Challenge Event -> Operational Lesson asks which subject is challenged. It requires a challenges Relation Kind proposal rather than being compressed into evidence-bears-on or declares-effect-on.
Ontology Node -> governed subject through represents may remain ontology-local. It cannot be published as a global identity assertion.

A Capability Realization Binding may remain the canonical lifecycle record and project one digest-bound implementation -> product-capability Typed Relation. The projection cannot become a second writable authority.
The undeclared pair experiment-run -> product remains rejected even when both endpoints exist and another membership pair is admitted.
domain_context.explanation: CyberAlchemy Lab keeps global Relation Kind contracts closed as exact ordered endpoint pairs. A proposal resolves the effective predecessor, proves endpoint carrier or internal-record contracts, preserves one semantic question, binds pair-specific qualifier rules and contestability, selects canonical relation authority, passes orthogonality and no-collapse validation, and submits the exact successor contract for admission. Ontology-local edges remain local unless an independently admitted global contract exists. The proposal has no effect while candidate-only.

plain_language.explanation: A new kind of wire must name its two plug types, purpose, labels, owner, challenge route, and one authoritative record. Both plug contracts must exist. A wire drawn only inside one Ontology stays local. Adding a plug, copying a local wire, or validating a draft does not connect anything globally.

boundary_conditions: Conn(r) contains ordered endpoint-kind pairs, so (s,t) and (t,s) are distinct unless both are explicitly declared.
SourceKinds(r) and TargetKinds(r) are generated projections of Conn(r); they do not authorize SourceKinds(r) x TargetKinds(r).
The effective predecessor version must be resolved through exact decision and succession overlays before a successor pair set is computed.
Both endpoint kinds must resolve to admitted carriers or explicitly permitted governed internal record contracts.
Each pair binds a qualifier schema, allowed values, and cross-qualifier constraints; open qualifier strings do not close the connection contract.
One canonical relation authority is selected. A specialized carrier projection and generic Typed Relation cannot both accept independent writes.
Global and ontology-local scope are distinct. Local(o,s,t) supplies no global pair.
Every effective contract supplies contestability, owner, evidence, lifecycle, and authority-effect boundaries.
Only an exact admitted successor Relation Kind contract makes a proposed global pair available.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: For each global Relation Kind r, Conn(r) is a finite closed set of ordered pairs (s,t) in K x K. ValidExtend(r@v,s,t,r@v_prime) requires Effective(r@v), Resolved(s), Resolved(t), SameQuestion(r@v,r@v_prime), PairQualifierSchema(r@v_prime,s,t), CanonicalAuthority(r@v_prime,s,t) in {TypedRelation, SpecializedCarrier}, Contestable(r@v_prime,s,t), and exact owner, evidence, lifecycle, validation, and successor bindings. A relation instance e conforms only when (kind(source(e)),kind(target(e))) is in Conn(r@v_prime), direction and qualifiers validate, and the exact contract is admitted and effective. Local(o,s,t) does not imply (s,t) in Conn(r). Register(k) does not imply any (k,x) or (x,k) in Conn(r).
scientific_formal.normative_statement: The Typed Connection Extension Rule requires every global Relation Kind to expose a finite closed set of exact ordered source-kind to target-kind connections. A proposed extension must bind one effective predecessor Relation Kind version, one source endpoint contract, one target endpoint contract, direction, global scope, an exact qualifier schema with pair-specific values and constraints, canonical relation authority, contestability, owner, evidence, lifecycle effect, validation effect, and the exact successor contract version. It may reuse the Relation Kind only when the same unique semantic question remains intact; otherwise it must propose a distinct Relation Kind. Ontology-local connections must remain scoped to their exact Ontology contract. No global connection is created by endpoint registration, separate source and target lists, wildcard matching, historical observation, local graph use, shared naming, candidate validation, endpoint admission, or a second writable projection.
